draft.title: The unit circle
card: The unit circle has its centre at the origin and radius 1. Start at the point (1, 0) and turn anticlockwise by an angle θ. You land on a point P on the circle.
The x-coordinate of P is cos θ. The y-coordinate of P is sin θ. So P = (cos θ, sin θ).

Signs follow from the coordinates. In quadrant 1, x and y are both positive. In quadrant 2, x is negative and y is positive. In quadrant 3, both are negative. In quadrant 4, x is positive and y is negative.
Example: at θ = 90°, P = (0, 1), so cos 90° = 0 and sin 90° = 1. At θ = 180°, P = (−1, 0), so cos 180° = −1 and sin 180° = 0.
draft.remember: On the unit circle, P = (cos θ, sin θ), so the signs of x and y give the signs of cos θ and sin θ.

a.q: What is the value of sin 180°?
a.why: At 180° the point on the unit circle is (−1, 0). Sin is the y-coordinate, so sin 180° = 0. The value −1 is the x-coordinate, which is cos 180°.
a.clue: Sin is one of the two coordinates. Which one?

b.q: An angle θ has its point P on the unit circle in quadrant 3. Which pair of signs is correct?
opts: cos θ is negative and sin θ is negative
cos θ is negative and sin θ is positive
cos θ is positive and sin θ is negative
cos θ is positive and sin θ is positive
b.why: In quadrant 3, P is to the left of the y-axis and below the x-axis, so x and y are both negative. Cos θ is x and sin θ is y, so both are negative. Quadrant 2 is the one where only cos θ is negative.
b.clue: Think about which side of each axis quadrant 3 lies on.

b.best: cos θ is negative and sin θ is negative

final.title: The unit circle
card: The unit circle has its centre at the origin and radius 1. Start at the point \((1, 0)\) and turn anticlockwise by an angle \(\theta\). You land on a point \(P\) on the circle.
The x-coordinate of \(P\) is \(\cos \theta\). The y-coordinate of \(P\) is \(\sin \theta\). So \(P = (\cos \theta, \sin \theta)\).

Signs follow from the coordinates. In quadrant 1, \(x\) and \(y\) are both positive. In quadrant 2, \(x\) is negative and \(y\) is positive. In quadrant 3, both are negative. In quadrant 4, \(x\) is positive and \(y\) is negative.

2.alt: The unit circle, centre the origin and radius 1. Turning anticlockwise by \(\theta\) from \((1, 0)\), shown by the small arc with an arrow, reaches the point \(P\). Dashed lines from \(P\) to the axes show its x-coordinate, \(\cos \theta\), and its y-coordinate, \(\sin \theta\).

final.remember: On the unit circle, \(P = (\cos \theta, \sin \theta)\), so the signs of \(x\) and \(y\) give the signs of \(\cos \theta\) and \(\sin \theta\).

a.why: At 180° the point on the unit circle is \((-1, 0)\). Sin is the y-coordinate, so \(\sin 180^{\circ} = 0\). The value \(-1\) is the x-coordinate, which is \(\cos 180^{\circ}\).
a.clue: Sin is one of the two coordinates. Which one?

b.q: An angle \(\theta\) has its point \(P\) on the unit circle in quadrant 3. Which pair of signs is correct?
b.why: In quadrant 3, \(P\) is to the left of the y-axis and below the x-axis, so \(x\) and \(y\) are both negative. Cos is \(x\) and sin is \(y\), so \(\cos \theta\) and \(\sin \theta\) are both negative. Quadrant 2 is the one where only \(\cos \theta\) is negative.
b.clue: Think about which side of each axis quadrant 3 lies on.

problems: The label (1, 0) is squeezed between the dashed guide from P and the circle, and its opening bracket touches the dashed line in both light and dark, so it reads as crowded and could be taken as labelling where the guide meets the x-axis; place it below-right or right of its dot, clear of the guide.
The angle theta has no arc from the positive x-axis to the radius, so the turn anticlockwise from (1, 0) that the card describes is not shown; add a small arc (ideally with an arrowhead) for theta.

pictures.brief: The unit circle, centre the origin and radius 1, on equal scales, with (1, 0) marked below-right of its dot, clear of the dashed guide. A radius from the origin to P at about 50 degrees, labelled 1 on its upper-left side. A small arc with an arrowhead from the positive x-axis up to the radius, showing the turn theta anticlockwise. The label theta sits inside the angle, between the x-axis and the radius, to the right of the arc (near (0.35, 0.15)), on the correct side of the radius, never between the radius and the y-axis. Dashed guides from P to the axes, labelled cos theta on the x-axis and sin theta on the y-axis.
